       I.      INTRODUCTION

           Scimitar Partners LP and Bar H Bar Land & Cattle Co. (collectively, “Bar H Bar Ranch

and Nature Preserve” or “ranch”) provides this Initial Brief regarding Oncor Electric Delivery

Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation (“LCRA”) (collectively,

“Joint Applicants”) proposed 765-kilovolt (“kV”) transmission line from the Bell County East

Switch to the Big Hill Substation. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve is concerned that certain

routing links, specifically links H1 and G52, would substantially affect ranching and preservation

efforts on the ranch and require significant reductions in the area usable on the ranch for both. The

Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve, as opposed to most of the ranches and properties affected

in this proceeding, is a unique property. This Initial Brief will go into great detail about the unique

features that define the Ranch and why the impact to the Ranch is substantially greater than it

would be to other ranches and properties subject to possible placement of the transmission line.

Further, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve will provide evidence in this Initial Brief that the

cost estimates related to the use of links H1 and G52 have been significantly undervalued by Joint

Applicants, and that use of either link will substantially increase the cost of any route that utilizes

said links. Therefore, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve would oppose the selection of any

route that includes links H1 and G52, including route 894.

           Joint Applicants have recommended route 8941 as the route that best meets the routing

criteria outlined in the Public Utility Regulatory Act 2 (“PURA”) and route 894 utilizes both links

H1 and G52. Further, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve is aware that other intervenors have

proposed various alternative routes that do not utilize the above-mentioned links. Bar H Bar Ranch

          II.      FACTUAL BACKGROUND


                A defining feature of the Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve is the unique role it plays

in the community. The Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve is a sprawling 3,815-acre ranch 3 in

the heart of the Texas Hill Country that is home to over thirty species of various animals including

both endangered and protected species. 4 One of the most impactful aspects of Bar H Bar Ranch

and Nature Preserve is the intentional commitment to maintaining a truly free-range environment

with no true interior fencing.5 Across the nearly 4,000 acres, animals are able to roam naturally,

establish territory, interact within healthy herd dynamics, and behave much as they would in the

wild.6 This approach creates a more natural ecosystem and reduces the stress and behavioral

limitations often associated with heavily segmented ranch environments. 7 Equally important is the

                          1. Community Values

              Community values are not defined in statute, rule, or by Commission precedent, but can

generally be understood as the values shared appreciation of an area or other natural or human

resource by members of a national, regional, or local community. The Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature

Preserve provides a unique ranch in the community that prioritizes the health and safety of the

various animals, including endangered species, on the property while also allowing members of

                                         i.       Habitable Structures

           As a component of the PUCT's consideration of the community values impact of a

proposed transmission line project pursuant to the provisions of PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A), the

Commission requires utility applicants to identify the number of habitable structures within 500

feet of a project of this voltage (i.e., greater than 230 kV). There is no magic to the distance of

500 feet, it is the arbitrary distance established in the PUCT's rules for notice and application

purposes. The rule’s Prudent Avoidance definition does not include this 500 foot criteria; indeed,

the only mentions of habitable structures within 500 feet of a centerline relate to notice or who can

settle a CCN case without applying all the rule criteria. 17 Unfortunately, as a result of those

requirements, a potentially significant level of attention is given to structures within 500 feet while

others that are slightly further than 500 feet away, which will face exposures and other adverse

transmission line impacts, are generally excluded from much consideration. 18

           Another factor to consider regarding habitable structures is the reasoning behind the 500

feet metric, which would include health and safety concerns with setbacks for fall height rules for

the tower structures and line blow down, and prudent setbacks from electromagnetic fields

(“EMF”) and energy shedding from the high voltage transmission lines. It is not reasonable to

assume that a 230-kV transmission line as stated as the minimum standard in the PURA rules,

would hold the same level of safety concern as the much larger 765kV lines. 19 The sheer size and

                                         ii.      Airstrips and Helipads

options in case of emergencies if links H1 or G52 are constructed. 29 In fact, given the configuration

of the Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve holdings, no helipad sites would be viable or

functional post construction of Links G52 and H1, given the LZ’s would not realistically be able

providing a sprawling ranch where members of the community can engage with protected and

endangered species, it also employs members of the community to maintain and operate the ranch.

The ranch also has three full-time employees that are not members of the combined

Hinckley/Bracht family, as well as employing multiple members of the Hinckley/Bracht family

that run the ranch.34 Two of those three outside employees live on the ranch, and the ranch plays

a vital role in employing members of the community in Burnet and Lampasas counties. 35

Construction of links H1 and G52, as outlined extensively in this brief, would have a severe

             The Joint Applicants’ did not include any of the above species in their environmental

assessment42 and Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve thinks it is important to show the effects

this oversight would have on these population. To provide examples of the real work effects of

this, the Scimitar Horned Oryx is one of the strongest examples in the world of a species surviving

largely because of captive conservation outside its native range. 43 By the 1980s and early 1990s,

the species had effectively disappeared from the wild across its native North African range due to

civil unrest, expanding livestock pressure and habitat degradation. 44 The species was considered

Extinct in the Wild by the IUCN Red List — meaning no self-sustaining wild population remained

in its native habitat.45 At that point, the global survival of the species depended almost entirely on

captive populations held in zoological institutions, private conservation collections and especially

large private ranches in Texas and the American Southwest – like ours. Texas became uniquely

important because private ranches could maintain:


                       very large free-ranging herds,

                       healthy breeding populations,

                       broad genetic diversity,

                       and long-term habitat-scale management that zoos alone often could not provide. 46

             From a conservation management perspective, habitat fragmentation is one of the most

significant concerns for the ranch.60 The ranch has been intentionally designed to create

interconnected ecological zones that support multiple species with differing habitat needs.

Dividing the property with a large transmission corridor could reduce the effectiveness of these

habitat systems and diminish the natural free-range character that is central to the ranch’s operation

and conservation philosophy.61 The visual and environmental impact would also affect the overall

integrity of the ranch experience.62 Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve operates not only as a

wildlife management property, but also as a destination centered around natural landscapes,

conservation, ethical hunting, and immersion in an undisturbed ranch environment. Large-scale

transmission infrastructure would materially alter the scenic character, sense of seclusion, and

wilderness qualities that define the property. 63

            In addition, transmission infrastructure could create operational challenges involving:

wildlife movement and capture logistics, helicopter-assisted management operations, fencing and

pasture management, controlled habitat restoration efforts and future conservation planning. 64

            As has been outlined extensively in this brief already, there are significant historical and

children learned to appreciate the beauty of the Texas Hill Country as well as nature conservation

while growing up on the ranch over the past 26 years. 68 Sadly, Bill passed away earlier in 2026
